node-1.label: Progressively worsening dyspnea and diarrhea of 1 week's duration

node-2.label: Past medical history: end-stage renal disease status post–renal transplant, atrial fibrillation, and sick sinus syndrome status after dual-chamber pacemaker placement

node-3.label: Patient denied chest pain, palpitations, or syncope

node-4.label: Vital signs showed hypoxia requiring 4 L/min oxygen, blood pressure 130/79 mm Hg, and heart rate 90 bpm; physical examination revealed elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral pulmonary basilar crackles, and lower extremity pitting edema

why.why: Chest X-ray showing severe bilateral pulmonary congestion and echocardiography with LVEF 35% confirm cardiogenic volume overload. Both the radiologist and laboratory physician independently state that the imaging and clinical/laboratory evidence fully establish the diagnosis, with diarrhea explained by congestive gastroenteropathy and renal failure as a complication. Confidence raised from 0.93 to 0.95.

Both expert analyses explicitly exclude pulmonary embolism based on the absence of chest pain/syncope and the presence of hypervolemia with severe bilateral pulmonary congestion and reduced LVEF. Confidence lowered from 0.04 to 0.02.

Both expert analyses explicitly exclude gastroenteritis/dehydration; diarrhea is explained by congestive gastroenteropathy in the setting of confirmed volume overload. Confidence lowered from 0.02 to 0.01.

node-8.label: Chest X-ray shows severe bilateral pulmonary congestion

node-9.label: Echocardiography reveals left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% with normal regional wall motion

node-10.label: Laboratory tests show potassium 9.0 mmol/L and creatinine 2.8 mg/dL

node-11.label: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 35%) causing cardiogenic volume overload

why.why: Echocardiography demonstrates LVEF 35% with normal wall motion and chest X-ray shows severe bilateral pulmonary congestion, directly confirming systolic heart failure as the cause of volume overload. Both expert analyses conclude that the diagnosis is established even though BNP/troponin were not retrieved, so confidence is raised from 0.88 to 0.92.

node-12.label: Acute renal failure with severe hyperkalemia complicating cardiogenic volume overload

why.why: Potassium 9.0 mmol/L and creatinine 2.8 mg/dL in a patient with a renal transplant and cardiogenic volume overload indicate acute renal failure complicating the picture. The radiologist emphasizes acute renal failure as a complication, and the laboratory physician explicitly supports a cardiorenal presentation. Confidence raised from 0.8 to 0.85; slight uncertainty remains because baseline renal function and acuity are not fully specified.

node-13.label: Diarrhea is caused by congestive gastroenteropathy secondary to cardiogenic volume overload

attrs.why: The patient has confirmed cardiogenic volume overload with elevated JVP, edema, and severe pulmonary congestion; bowel wall congestion in this setting can produce diarrhea. The laboratory physician explicitly states that diarrhea is consistent with congestive gastroenteropathy, and gastroenteritis/dehydration is excluded by hypervolemia and imaging. Confidence is 0.7 because stool studies were not obtained.
